fact: The director general of the state company SDIN (Societe nationale de developpement des infrastructures numeriques) said at its HQ inauguration that it operates a national optical fibre network of more than 1,760 km on three main axes linking the country's regions; reported by AMI. The statement is dated 2025-12-16, the document's date.

The World Bank completion report says construction of five fibre-optic links in Mauritania was under way when the project closing date was extended on 2019-10-20 to allow completion of the fibre backbone links, after delays in signing the construction contract.

The World Bank says five fibre-optic links totalling 1,710 km were laid and became operational under WARCIP APL2, distributing international connectivity from the ACE landing to most provincial capitals and to the Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso and Morocco cross-border links; operators expanded 4G once the links were operational. Date taken as the project closing, 2021-11, the report (2022-08-26) giving no lighting date.

The World Bank says the backbone was built under a PPP and open-access model giving operators fair access to the infrastructure, with state vehicle SDIN established and an affermage contract with IMT signed; no named buyers of capacity are given. No event date is given, so the report's published date is used.

The ministry's representative says over 4,000 km of the national optical fibre network has been completed, added to over 3,000 km by national operators for a 7,000 km total, with tenders prepared for 3,000 km more.
